speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically regarding the location and nature of your neck and arm pain, and when you first noticed the paresthesias and muscle weakness.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy / Cervical Radiculopathy.

Given your history of burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness over the last three months, along with your diabetes, I need to confirm the severity of the motor deficit. Are you experiencing difficulty with fine motor tasks, such as buttoning shirts or holding objects? Additionally, do you notice any changes in your balance, walking stability, or bowel/bladder control?
